name: Ruben II, Prince of Armenia
summary:
Ruben II, Prince of Armenia (ruben-ii-prince-of-armenia) was a significant lord of Armenian Cilicia from 1169 to 1170. He played a crucial role in the governance of the region during this period.

 As the seventh lord of Armenian Cilicia, Ruben II oversaw the administration of the territory, which included the cities of Sis and Artazoc.

 His reign was marked by several key events, including the establishment of trade relations with neighboring kingdoms and the development of a strong military presence in the region. Ruben II's leadership helped to maintain stability and security in Armenian Cilicia during a time of great turmoil in the region.

 Despite his efforts, Ruben II's reign was cut short when he died in 1169, marking the end of an era for the lordship of Armenian Cilicia.

 The legacy of Ruben II can be seen in the continued development of Armenian Cilicia as a major power in the region, and his leadership played a significant role in shaping the course of history in this area.
